service_requests.function: Routers and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: Firewall/Router for the H.S. Annex 'Sacred Heart Gym'.Layer 3 aggregation switch for MS, HS, LHLC and WP Elementary. Must have minimum 16 SFP28 slots capable of communicating at either 10Gbs or 25Gbs, and a minimum of 2 QSFP28 ports capable of communication at 100Gbps or 25Gbps. Must have redundant power supply.3 Layer 3 switches with minimum of 16 SFP28 ports capable of 25Gbs and 10Gbs speeds.6 Layer 2 switches with 48 ethernet ports capable of minimum 2.5 Gbe speeds, and a minimum 32 ports capable of 10Gbe speeds. All ports must be capable of POE+++ power delivery. Minimum of four SFP28 ports capable of 25Gbs speeds.4 Layer 2 switches with 24 ethernet ports capable of 2.5 Gbs speeds, at least 8 capable of 10Gbs speeds, and have a minimum of 2x SFP28 ports capble of 25Gbs and 10Gbs speeds.35x access points. Must support WiFi 7 protocols (802.11be), must be capable of 10Gbp uplink speeds, and support 10 WiFi streams. (4x 6Ghz, 4x 5Ghz and 2x 2.4Ghz radios).

service_requests.description: Library requests bids for equipment, services, and licensing for Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) to support management of the library's broadband network.Requested functionality includes:- Ability to establish bandwidth quotas for individual devices/users.- Ability to monitor and track broadband usage for the entire network and individual devices/users.- Ability to prioritize, limit, or block broadband access for individual devices.- Content filtering and malware-blocking functionality. Any ineligible content-filtering or other ineligible functionality must be separately identified and priced.- Equipment, software, and licensing necessary to provide the proposed MIBS solution.- For all proposed equipment, bids must provide the manufacturer, model, and SKU/part number, as applicable.Pricing RequirementsBids must include all applicable fees and charges associated with the proposed solution, including:- Equipment costs.- Licensing/subscription costs.- Monthly recurring charges.- One-time/non-recurring charges.- Installation, configuration, and activation charges.- Equipment rental or other applicable charges.- Any other fees or charges necessary to implement and operate the proposed solution.The cost of E-Rate-eligible services/equipment must be separated from the cost of ineligible services/equipment. If licensing is separately priced and is necessary for the operation of the proposed equipment or service, the licensing and associated cost must be clearly identified in the bid.Bids must provide sufficient information for the applicant to determine the total cost of the proposed solution.One-year and multi-year pricing may be submitted; however, a one-year pricing option is required.Vendors may bid on Category 1 and/or Category 2 MIBS services/equipment. If a vendor proposes both Category 1 Internet service and associated Category 2 MIBS, the bid must clearly identify whether the Category 2 service/equipment is required as a condition of obtaining the proposed Category 1 service. Category 1 and Category 2 costs must be separately identified.Bid Requirements and Disqualifying FactorsTo be considered responsive:- The bid must specifically address the services and requirements identified in this FCC Form 470.- The bid must reference this specific FCC Form 470 and provide a proposed solution responsive to the applicant's specific requirements.- For all proposed equipment, the bid must identify the manufacturer, model, and SKU/part number, as applicable.- The bid must include complete pricing, including all applicable fees and charges.- Eligible and ineligible costs must be separately identified.- The bidder must have a valid SPIN/498 ID.- The bidder must be willing to provide discounted billing and invoice USAC using the Service Provider Invoice (SPI) method.- The bid must be received no later than 30 calendar days after the FCC Form 470 is posted.Generic advertisements, flyers, marketing materials, mass-distributed solicitations, generic price lists, SPAM/robobids, automated responses, or other responses that do not specifically address this FCC Form 470 and the applicant's requested services will be considered non-responsive and will be disqualified from consideration.Bids that do not provide the required manufacturer/model/SKU information, complete pricing, or all applicable fees and charges, or that require the applicant to contact the bidder to obtain basic pricing or determine what equipment/service is being proposed will be considered non-responsive and will be disqualified from consideration.Bids received after the stated 30-calendar-day deadline will be disqualified from consideration.

Any addendums that are issued will be on the Customers web page. The Vendor shall be responsible for all parts, labor, and all other associated apparatus necessary to completely install, test, and turnover for acceptance to the Customer the project detailed herein. The building that the district is looking for replacement in are as follows: Michigan Center High School. Requested project includes: remove the current wall mounted cabinet in A128 (Science Classroom) and replace with a cabinet of the same size. Reterminate and dress all cabling as needed. Size of existing cabinet: 23W x 36H x 27D, 22U.The Vendor shall provide equipment, materials, labor, and services to provide data distribution system including, but not limited to:1. Raceway, boxes, cable tray and similar cable supporting devices. (J-hooks)2. Data cabling terminations.3. Optical fiber and terminations.4. Telecommunications outlets.5. Terminal blocks/cross-connect systems and fire-retardant mounting board. (Telephone vendor will provide punch-down services to terminate voice cross-connect cables).6. Equipment racks and cabinets.7. System testing.8. Documentation and submissions.9. Any necessary pathwayVendor will provide all equipment, materials, labor and services, not specifically mentioned or shown, which may be necessary to complete or perfect all parts of the installation.Timeline: Intent To Bid Form Deadline - October 22, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. Required Vendor Site Visit - October 26, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. RFP Technical Questions Deadline  November 6, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Proposal Due Date and bid opening  November 20, 2026 at 1:00 p.m.The sole point of contact concerning this solicitation is: Brad HessJackson County Intermediate School District6700 Browns Lake RoadJackson, MI 49201Attn: Michigan Center Network Cabinet Upgrade Proposals must be delivered to Brad Hess, and received prior to this deadline to the address noted above. E-mails will be accepted. Submit email responses to [redacted] Vendors must have an E-rate SPIN designation, please include the SPIN# in your response.Specifications and requirements are included in the attached RFP. This RFP packet will be available on our website at the following link, http://www.jcisd.org, under the About Us/Proposals/Bids tab. Vendors are responsible for obtaining any updates or amendments to the RFP from the website.

service_requests.description: Four Star Public Library District seeks bids for Category Two Internal Connections equipment and installation to upgrade network security and expand wireless connectivity within its approximately 4,500-square-foot library facility.Requested equipment includes one 12-port vertical-mount patch panel; 11 CAT6 RJ45 HD keystone connectors; 11 six-foot CAT6 Ethernet patch cables; approximately 675 feet of CAT6 plenum-rated bulk Ethernet cable; one Ubiquiti UniFi Cloud Gateway Ultra (or equivalent) to replace an unsupported USG firewall; and one Ubiquiti U6 Pro wireless access point (or equivalent) to provide Wi-Fi coverage in the library's community room.The project includes approximately 20 hours of installation, cabling, configuration, and testing labor. Vendors should provide itemized pricing for equipment, materials, and installation, identifying E-Rate eligible and ineligible costs separately. Equivalent equipment meeting the library's functional requirements will be considered.

service_requests.description: Please review RFP carefully.  Please reference 470# 270002178 on all correspondence.Please note: USAC has advised applicants to include all three types of service on each Category 2 Form 470. MIBS was listed above in case USAC deems anything to fit that category.Western Wayne Schools (the Applicant) is seeking proposals for a project to supply and install structured cabling at two eligible sites.  Bidders are advised that this project will be contingent upon district approval and the successful obtaining of Category 2 E-Rate funding, and the contract agreement between the Applicant and the successful bidder must recognize that contingency.  Bidders should also understand that this RFP is essentially for time and materials pricing and the district reserves the right to scale this project back substantially or to cancel it entirely, regardless of the status of E-Rate funding.Project ScopeContractor will supply pricing for time and materials to install up to a total of 72 +/- Category 6A  plenum cable runs, each of an average of 250 at the schools listed below, terminated in a combination of Owner or Vendor supplied patch panels in IDF/MDF.  The contractor shall provide and install all equipment, materials, cabling, hardware and labor required to deliver a complete and fully functional network cabling infrastructure and a computer (data) network cabling infrastructure as specified.  All terminations shall meet or exceed Category 6A ratings.**Lincoln Middle High School215 E Parkway DrCambridge City, IN 47327: 47 +/- runs**Western Wayne Elementary School801 E Delaware StCambridge City, IN 47327; 25 +/- runsThis cabling will replace existing aging cabling infrastructure. The awarded contractor will be responsible for removing the cabling runs being replaced.Most runs are in open or drop ceilings and can be reached via ladder, though a few will require a lift to install.  Cables should be in cable tray where available, and otherwise suspended every 4 feet in drop ceilings using J or D style hooks or in enclosed conduit on exterior runs.  The contractor shall not tie or suspend wiring to sprinkler pipes, electrical conduits or insulated ceiling joists.  Under no circumstances shall wiring be laid on or across ceiling tiles.Runs to WAP locations will be terminated in single-gang above-ceiling boxes with a 6 service loop left neatly coiled and supported above the ceiling on each end of the run.All cabling and hardware at all locations shall be Panduit product or General Cable (Prysmian Group) product or equivalent. All installed cabling will be labeled on both termination points. Cable labeling schema, cable colors, and faceplate jack colors must be coordinated with owner.Wiring which requires routing through steel walls or other abrasive surfaces shall be protected using rubber grommets, conduit sleeves or other appropriate protective devices.  Holes around conduit sleeves which penetrate between floors, walls and ceilings shall be completely filled with matching material. All wiring penetrations through fire-rated walls, floors or ceilings shall be completely filled with fire-rated caulk. All horizontal wiring shall run parallel to walls. Turns and room entries shall make ninety (90) degree angles while maintaining the manufacturers minimum specified bend radius.  The contractor shall make themselves aware of all adjacent AC power and other high voltage circuits so as to give adequate separation between high and low voltage wiring.Vendor must have BICSI RCDD on staff. Vendor must have at least one BICSI technician or installer on staff. Vendor must test the cable plant with a Fluke DTX tester or equivalent and provide electronic test results. Installation, testing and labeling is to be done in a professional manner and must be in accordance with the current TIA/EIA Telecommunications Building Wiring Standards. Wiring shall meet or exceed all state and local electrical codes.  It is the responsibility of the contractor to remove all debris from the project site.  All areas shall be wiped clean and floors broom swept clean.Documentation and as-built drawings must be provided at the owners request.Questions/Site VisitsA voluntary site visit will be held at Lincoln Middle High School, 215 E Parkway Dr, Cambridge City, IN 47327, in the Multipurpose room (Please enter through Door 29 on the back side of the building, at the east end of the football field off Lincoln Drive) at 1:00PM (EST) on October 30, 2026.  This will be the only opportunity to ask questions or to receive answers to questions related to this RFP.  Respondents choosing not to attend in so doing acknowledge their understanding that they were offered and voluntarily declined the opportunity.Building drawings may be requested via e-mail to the contact above.  For security reasons, this is the only way to get these drawings.

Bidders should also understand that this RFP is essentially for time and materials pricing and the district reserves the right to scale this project back substantially or to cancel it entirely, regardless of the status of E-Rate funding.Project ScopeContractor will supply pricing for time and materials to install up to a total of 72 +/- Category 6A  plenum cable runs, each of an average of 250 at the schools listed below, terminated in a combination of Owner or Vendor supplied patch panels in IDF/MDF.  The contractor shall provide and install all equipment, materials, cabling, hardware and labor required to deliver a complete and fully functional network cabling infrastructure and a computer (data) network cabling infrastructure as specified.  All terminations shall meet or exceed Category 6A ratings.**Lincoln Middle High School215 E Parkway DrCambridge City, IN 47327: 47 +/- runs**Western Wayne Elementary School801 E Delaware StCambridge City, IN 47327; 25 +/- runsThis cabling will replace existing aging cabling infrastructure. The awarded contractor will be responsible for removing the cabling runs being replaced.Most runs are in open or drop ceilings and can be reached via ladder, though a few will require a lift to install.  Cables should be in cable tray where available, and otherwise suspended every 4 feet in drop ceilings using J or D style hooks or in enclosed conduit on exterior runs.  The contractor shall not tie or suspend wiring to sprinkler pipes, electrical conduits or insulated ceiling joists.  Under no circumstances shall wiring be laid on or across ceiling tiles.Runs to WAP locations will be terminated in single-gang above-ceiling boxes with a 6 service loop left neatly coiled and supported above the ceiling on each end of the run.All cabling and hardware at all locations shall be Panduit product or General Cable (Prysmian Group) product or equivalent. All installed cabling will be labeled on both termination points. Cable labeling schema, cable colors, and faceplate jack colors must be coordinated with owner.Wiring which requires routing through steel walls or other abrasive surfaces shall be protected using rubber grommets, conduit sleeves or other appropriate protective devices.  Holes around conduit sleeves which penetrate between floors, walls and ceilings shall be completely filled with matching material. All wiring penetrations through fire-rated walls, floors or ceilings shall be completely filled with fire-rated caulk. All horizontal wiring shall run parallel to walls. Turns and room entries shall make ninety (90) degree angles while maintaining the manufacturers minimum specified bend radius.  The contractor shall make themselves aware of all adjacent AC power and other high voltage circuits so as to give adequate separation between high and low voltage wiring.Vendor must have BICSI RCDD on staff. Vendor must have at least one BICSI technician or installer on staff. Vendor must test the cable plant with a Fluke DTX tester or equivalent and provide electronic test results. Installation, testing and labeling is to be done in a professional manner and must be in accordance with the current TIA/EIA Telecommunications Building Wiring Standards. Wiring shall meet or exceed all state and local electrical codes.  It is the responsibility of the contractor to remove all debris from the project site.  All areas shall be wiped clean and floors broom swept clean.Documentation and as-built drawings must be provided at the owners request.Questions/Site VisitsA voluntary site visit will be held at Lincoln Middle High School, 215 E Parkway Dr, Cambridge City, IN 47327, in the Multipurpose room (Please enter through Door 29 on the back side of the building, at the east end of the football field off Lincoln Drive) at 1:00PM (EST) on October 30, 2026.  This will be the only opportunity to ask questions or to receive answers to questions related to this RFP.  Respondents choosing not to attend in so doing acknowledge their understanding that they were offered and voluntarily declined the opportunity.Building drawings may be requested via e-mail to the contact above.  For security reasons, this is the only way to get these drawings.

YOU MUST REFER TO THE ASSOCIATED RFP Document in EPC for compete details. This is not a formal "RFP," but provides details which should allow service providers to prepare more directed bids. It is important that service providers read the attached document to fully understand this project and prepare a more directed bid. Service Providers are responsible for monitoring the USAC EPC site for any updates to this posting.-----East Knox Local School District (the Applicant) seeks services provided by a third party for the operation, management, and monitoring of eligible broadband LAN/WLAN components (managed Wi-Fi).  We seek a 5+/- year contract with or without the option of voluntary extensions for eligible MIBS services under this agreement.  The Applicant understands that eligible Basic Maintenance of Internal Connections items are also sometimes necessary to provision a Managed Internal Broadband service, and expects bidders to propose those as necessary. Services are to start July 1, 2027 with the beginning of the 2027 ERate funding year. Bidders are advised that this project will be contingent upon the successful obtaining of Category 2 E-Rate funding, and the contract agreement between the district and the successful bidder must recognize that contingency.  Proposals must separate eligible and ineligible services by line item for all services to which service provider responds. Please break down pricing by building.-----Applicant owns this equipment and is not considering proposals for the purchase of new equipment at this time.  In your proposal, please also provide per-unit pricing for the management of growth/future additions of equipment similar to the equipment requested above in the contract.  For clarity, this is to say that if the Applicant asked in this RFP for a bid to manage 30 access points, your proposal would include pricing to manage those 30 access points for the term requested, and also include the incremental additional (per-unit) price that would be charged to add that unit to management under this contract should the Applicant add a 31st (or 32nd, etc.) access point during the term of the agreement.  This is merely an example; please refer to the equipment list above for the actual equipment for which management services are requested. The district may require support of alternative equipment other than outlined in the RFP, that equipment will be equivalent makes and models and will serve a similar functionality, see RFP. NOTE: Leased services MIBS has been included in the Services Requests Section above. While it is not the intention of the District to lease equipment, this has been added "just in case" a vendor needs to add or provision any equipment for complete service.-----QUESTIONSNo informational meetings or building visits will be scheduled.   Any questions related to the technical aspects of this document should be directed to Jessica Busenburg, Treasurer at [redacted], no later than 2:00 pm (EST) on 11-4-2026. All emails must include reference to FCC Form 470 270002282 in the subject line of the email. Answers to any written questions or any additional information, revisions, or clarifications to the RFP will be provided in the form of an addendum to be posted with the FCC Form 470 on the Universal Service (E-Rate) website.  It is the sole responsibility of the Service Provider to check for any addenda that may be issued.-----PROPOSAL DELIVERYThe Applicant reserves the right to reject each and every bid, and to waive informalities, irregularities, and errors in the bidding to the extent permitted by law.  This includes the right to extend the date and time for receipt of bids.  In the event that a responsible bid is not received or if it is determined that the low bid received is too high, the bid received will be rejected and the project will be cancelled or re-bid. Bid should be emailed to the office of Jessica Busenburg, Treasurer, at [redacted], by 12-09-2026 at 2:00 pm (EST). Bids received after that time will be disqualified. All emails must include reference to FCC Form 470 270002282 in the subject line of the email.  FAXED bids are not acceptable and will be rejected as non-responsive.

service_requests.function: Internet Access and Data Transmission Service
Switches and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: The District is seeking proposals to replace core network switches in the high school and Millcreek Elementary buildings. Each building requires a switch stack or equivalent solution that provides coordinated management, interswitch connectivity, and the port capacity specified below.Minimum Ethernet Port RequirementsThe high school requires a minimum of 180 usable RJ45 Ethernet ports. At least 40 ports must support 10 Gb multigigabit Ethernet with Class 6 PoE or better. The remaining 140 ports must support at least 1 Gbps Ethernet with Class 4 PoE or better.Millcreek Elementary requires a minimum of 170 usable RJ45 Ethernet ports. At least 50 ports must support 10 Gb multigigabit Ethernet with Class 6 PoE or better. The remaining 120 ports must support at least 1 Gbps Ethernet with Class 4 PoE or better.The multigigabit ports must support 1, 2.5, 5, and 10 Gbps Ethernet speeds and provide IEEE 802.3bt Class 6 PoE or better. The 1 Gb ports must provide IEEE 802.3at Class 4 PoE or better. Ports exceeding these minimum speed or PoE requirements are acceptable.Port quantities represent minimum usable connections at each building. Proposals may exceed the specified quantities to accommodate standard switch configurations. Fiber uplink ports and ports used for stacking or interswitch connections must be provided in addition to the required usable RJ45 Ethernet ports.Minimum Fiber Connectivity RequirementsThe high school solution must include at least one individual switch capable of supporting eight simultaneous 10 Gbps SFP+ fiber connections and another individual switch capable of supporting 2 simultaneous 10 Gbps SFP+ fiber connectionsThe Millcreek Elementary solution must include one switch capable of supporting at least two simultaneous 10 Gbps SFP+ fiber connections and a separate switch capable of supporting at least four simultaneous 10 Gbps SFP+ fiber connections.These fiber connections must remain available for network use after any ports required for stacking or interswitch connectivity are allocated. Bidders must identify the switch models and any expansion modules needed to meet these requirements.Configuration and CompatibilityEach proposed solution must support the Districts existing network functions, including applicable VLAN and routing requirements. Bidders must describe the proposed stack or equivalent architecture, interswitch bandwidth, management approach, and redundancy features.Proposals must identify the PoE budget available on each switch and across each buildings proposed configuration, including any limitations on simultaneously powering devices at the specified PoE classes. All power supplies necessary for the proposed configuration must be included.Proposal RequirementsProposals must include an itemized bill of materials identifying switch quantities, manufacturer and model numbers, port capabilities, uplink modules, power supplies, stacking components, cables, and required software licenses. Bidders must identify licensing terms, recurring costs, warranty coverage, support options, and anticipated delivery dates.Bidders must clearly state whether fiber transceivers are included or existing transceivers will be reused. Any proposed transceivers must be identified by type and compatibility with the Districts existing fiber infrastructure.Equipment, required licensing, installation or configuration services, and optional support must be priced separately. Any E-Rate-ineligible items or portions of costs must be clearly identified. Proposals must disclose all exceptions to the requested specifications.The District will consider equivalent solutions that meet or exceed these requirements.

service_requests.function: Internet Access and Data Transmission Service
service_requests.description: Library requests bids for equipment, services, and licensing for Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) to support management of the library's broadband network.Requested functionality includes:- Ability to establish bandwidth quotas for individual devices/users.- Ability to monitor and track broadband usage for the entire network and individual devices/users.- Ability to prioritize, limit, or block broadband access for individual devices.- Content filtering and malware-blocking functionality. Any ineligible content-filtering or other ineligible functionality must be separately identified and priced.- Equipment, software, and licensing necessary to provide the proposed MIBS solution.- For all proposed equipment, bids must provide the manufacturer, model, and SKU/part number, as applicable.Pricing RequirementsBids must include all applicable fees and charges associated with the proposed solution, including:- Equipment costs.- Licensing/subscription costs.- Monthly recurring charges.- One-time/non-recurring charges.- Installation, configuration, and activation charges.- Equipment rental or other applicable charges.- Any other fees or charges necessary to implement and operate the proposed solution.The cost of E-Rate-eligible services/equipment must be separated from the cost of ineligible services/equipment. If licensing is separately priced and is necessary for the operation of the proposed equipment or service, the licensing and associated cost must be clearly identified in the bid.Bids must provide sufficient information for the applicant to determine the total cost of the proposed solution.One-year and multi-year pricing may be submitted; however, a one-year pricing option is required.Vendors may bid on Category 1 and/or Category 2 MIBS services/equipment. If a vendor proposes both Category 1 Internet service and associated Category 2 MIBS, the bid must clearly identify whether the Category 2 service/equipment is required as a condition of obtaining the proposed Category 1 service. Category 1 and Category 2 costs must be separately identified.Bid Requirements and Disqualifying FactorsTo be considered responsive:- The bid must specifically address the services and requirements identified in this FCC Form 470.- The bid must reference this specific FCC Form 470 and provide a proposed solution responsive to the applicant's specific requirements.- For all proposed equipment, the bid must identify the manufacturer, model, and SKU/part number, as applicable.- The bid must include complete pricing, including all applicable fees and charges.- Eligible and ineligible costs must be separately identified.- The bidder must have a valid SPIN/498 ID.- The bidder must be willing to provide discounted billing and invoice USAC using the Service Provider Invoice (SPI) method.- The bid must be received no later than 30 calendar days after the FCC Form 470 is posted.Generic advertisements, flyers, marketing materials, mass-distributed solicitations, generic price lists, SPAM/robobids, automated responses, or other responses that do not specifically address this FCC Form 470 and the applicant's requested services will be considered non-responsive and will be disqualified from consideration.Bids that do not provide the required manufacturer/model/SKU information, complete pricing, or all applicable fees and charges, or that require the applicant to contact the bidder to obtain basic pricing or determine what equipment/service is being proposed will be considered non-responsive and will be disqualified from consideration.Bids received after the stated 30-calendar-day deadline will be disqualified from consideration.

service_requests.function: Switches and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: It is the intent of this form 470 to receive proposals from qualified vendors that are capable of the purchase of 24 port network switchesthat will be used to replace existing 24 port switches that are considered past end of life. The acquired switches will be used tosupport the existing Cranston Public Schools network for internet access. Licensing will not be required as the existing licenses will transfer ontothe replacement units. The scope of this project is to upgrade existing 24 port switches to accommodate the existinginfrastructure.Cranston is seeking vendors capable of providing equipment acquisition suited to integrate with the existing infrastructure.All vendors must adhere to the following Cranston Public Schools general bid conditions:1. AWARDS:Awards will be based on the following criteria and will be evaluated as such:Price of Eligible goods/services 30%Ability to integrate with existing infrastructure 30%Prior experience with District 20%Quality of Product 20%All awards are made subject to the availability of funds.2. SCHOOL COMMITTEE APPROVAL:The School Committee reserves the right to reject any and all bids or any part thereof or to accept such part or partsdeemed for the best interest of the Cranston Public Schools. The School Committee reserves the right to waive or refuseto waive informalities in bids.3. RHODE ISLAND SALES TAX:The Cranston Public Schools is exempt from the payment of the Rhode Island Sales Tax under the 1956 General Lawsof the State of Rhode Island, 44-18-30, Paragraph I, as amended.4. ADDENDA AND INTERPRETATIONS:No interpretation on the meaning of the Plans, Specifications or other Contract Document will be made to any bidderorally. Every request for such interpretations should be via email addressed to the Chief Technology Officer, Donna-Marie Frappier at [redacted]. All vendor inquiries will be addressed and shared with all vendors submittingproposals.

service_requests.description: Library requests bids for equipment, services, and licensing for Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) to support management of the library's broadband network.Requested functionality includes:- Ability to establish bandwidth quotas for individual devices/users.- Ability to monitor and track broadband usage for the entire network and individual devices/users.- Ability to prioritize, limit, or block broadband access for individual devices.- Content filtering and malware-blocking functionality. Any ineligible content-filtering or other ineligible functionality must be separately identified and priced.- Equipment, software, and licensing necessary to provide the proposed MIBS solution.- For all proposed equipment, bids must provide the manufacturer, model, and SKU/part number, as applicable.Pricing RequirementsBids must include all applicable fees and charges associated with the proposed solution, including:- Equipment costs.- Licensing/subscription costs.- Monthly recurring charges.- One-time/non-recurring charges.- Installation, configuration, and activation charges.- Equipment rental or other applicable charges.- Any other fees or charges necessary to implement and operate the proposed solution.The cost of E-Rate-eligible services/equipment must be separated from the cost of ineligible services/equipment. If licensing is separately priced and is necessary for the operation of the proposed equipment or service, the licensing and associated cost must be clearly identified in the bid.Bids must provide sufficient information for the applicant to determine the total cost of the proposed solution.One-year and multi-year pricing may be submitted; however, a one-year pricing option is required.Vendors may bid on Category 1 and/or Category 2 MIBS services/equipment. If a vendor proposes both Category 1 Internet service and associated Category 2 MIBS, the bid must clearly identify whether the Category 2 service/equipment is required as a condition of obtaining the proposed Category 1 service. Category 1 and Category 2 costs must be separately identified.Bid Requirements and Disqualifying FactorsTo be considered responsive:- The bid must specifically address the services and requirements identified in this FCC Form 470.- The bid must reference this specific FCC Form 470 and provide a proposed solution responsive to the applicant's specific requirements.- For all proposed equipment, the bid must identify the manufacturer, model, and SKU/part number, as applicable.- The bid must include complete pricing, including all applicable fees and charges.- Eligible and ineligible costs must be separately identified.- The bidder must have a valid SPIN/498 ID.- The bidder must be willing to provide discounted billing and invoice USAC using the Service Provider Invoice (SPI) method.- The bid must be received no later than 30 calendar days after the FCC Form 470 is posted.Generic advertisements, flyers, marketing materials, mass-distributed solicitations, generic price lists, SPAM/robobids, automated responses, or other responses that do not specifically address this FCC Form 470 and the applicant's requested services will be considered non-responsive and will be disqualified from consideration.Bids that do not provide the required manufacturer/model/SKU information, complete pricing, or all applicable fees and charges, or that require the applicant to contact the bidder to obtain basic pricing or determine what equipment/service is being proposed will be considered non-responsive and will be disqualified from consideration.Bids received after the stated 28-calendar-day deadline will be disqualified from consideration.

service_requests.function: Wireless Access Points and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: East Liverpool City Schools seeks proposals for a district-wide wireless network refresh across five school buildings and eligible campus instructional areas. The project includes indoor and outdoor wireless access points, wireless controllers/management, necessary software and licensing, cabling, mounting components, installation, configuration, and testing.Estimated maximum quantities: 400 wireless access points, 5 controllers, 400 related components, and 15,000 feet of cabling. Quantities are planning estimates, not required purchase amounts. Vendors shall assess existing infrastructure and propose a complete, appropriately sized solution meeting district coverage and capacity needs. Proposals must identify equipment models, quantities, unit pricing, installation costs, necessary licensing, and renewal costs. Centralized or distributed management solutions may be proposed. Equivalent manufacturers and solutions will be considered.MANDATORY SITE VISIT:Vendors must schedule an individual site walk-through with the district by emailing [redacted]. Appointments will be scheduled during normal business hours, subject to district availability, and must be completed by December 2, 2026. Vendors must assess existing infrastructure and determine the equipment and installation requirements for their proposed solution. Failure to complete the mandatory walk-through will result in disqualification. The district will provide prospective bidders reasonable opportunities to schedule visits.BIDDING REQUIREMENTS:All questions must be submitted in writing by November 30, 2026. Written answers and material clarifications will be made available equally to prospective bidders through EPC. Proposals must be emailed to [redacted] by December 10, 2026, at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Late proposals will be disqualified. Vendor selection and contract award will not occur before the applicable Allowable Contract Date and stated bid deadline.Bids will be evaluated using a weighted matrix, with the price of eligible products and services as the most heavily weighted factor. The district reserves the right to award all, part, or none of the requested services and to make separate awards where appropriate.DISQUALIFYING FACTORS:1. Failure to complete the mandatory site walk-through by December 2, 2026.2. Failure to submit a complete proposal with equipment descriptions, quantities, and itemized pricing by the stated deadline.3. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Bids must be received no later than 5:00 p.m. MST on the Allowable Contract Date (ACD).All vendors must complete and submit the E-Rate Service Provider Bid Response Worksheet with their proposal. Failure to submit the completed worksheet may result in disqualification. There will be no bidders conference, job walk, or product/service demonstrations, either in person or remotely.Vendors must comply with all requirements and specifications contained in the attached RFP and all associated solicitation documents. Quantities identified on FCC Form 470 are estimates only and do not constitute a commitment to purchase or guarantee that any quantity will be awarded.Vendors must not be debarred, suspended, or otherwise prohibited from participating in public procurement. Service providers are solely responsible for regularly monitoring the EPC Portal for updates, amendments, clarifications, and other information related to this solicitation. The Applicant will not be responsible for a vendors failure to review or receive information posted in the EPC Portal.

service_requests.description: District is seeking pricing for Internal Connections Network Equipment. For a complete description of the services being requested, please refer to the District issued RFP for FY2027: "26 27 03TE  Network Equipment"All prospective bidders are required to register with Planet Bids, at no cost to the Vendor.All inquiries or questions must be submitted via the Q&A feature on Planet Bids by November 12, 2026 at 12:00pm PST. The District will not respond to phone or email inquiries. All addendum(s), questions and answers will be posted to Planet Bids at https://pbsystem.planetbids.com/portal/60604/portal-home in addition to the E-rate EPC website at https://portal.usac.org/suite/2Bids will be received electronically through the Districts electronic bid management system Planet Bids, https://pbsystem.planetbids.com/portal/60604/portal-home. Bids are due by November 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM. It is the sole responsibility of the bidder to ensure that their bid arrives on time. The District is not responsible if the bid is not received by the due date. For full instructions on how to submit a bid, please refer to the District issued RFP.Due to the way EPC has been created with the service category questions, please consider information drafted into quantities, fields, and units as an educated guess at a minimum for the issuance of this Form 470 and RFP. All quantities are estimates as solutions proposed by vendors to meet the minimum specifications required may necessitate differing quantities. Please refer to the RFP for details on equipment/services being requested and all requirements. NOTE that the service types "Basic Maintenance of Internal Connections" (BMIC) and "Managed Internal Broadband Services" (MIBS) are only as applicable with the Internal Connections solution proposed meeting the RFP requirements. The District is not soliciting separate bids for BMIC or MIBS.To ensure that all Service Providers receive the same RFP information, it is required that you download the RFP directly from USACs EPC website , Planet Bids, or from the link in the posted Form 470. Please Follow this Form 470 to receive updates. SPAM and/or robotic responses will not be considered valid bid responses and will be disqualified from consideration.

East Liverpool City Schools seeks proposals for a district-wide network switching and infrastructure refresh across five school buildings and eligible instructional areas.The project includes replacement and upgrades of access, distribution, core, and aggregation switches, including switches located outside network closets in offices, classrooms, computer labs, and other eligible areas. The project also includes necessary software and licensing, fiber optics, SFP/SFP+ modules, DAC cables, stacking components, patch panels, network racks/cabinets, cable management, installation, configuration, and testing.The district has approximately 14 network closets (MDF/IDF locations). Existing patch panels are experiencing connector failures and require replacement. Vendors shall assess all network closets and identify damaged patch panels, required retermination, labeling, testing, and necessary rack or cabinet replacements. Replacement of existing in-wall cabling is not requested.Estimated maximum quantities:- 75 network switches, including access, core, aggregation, and smaller switches in offices, labs, and other eligible locations.- 30 network racks or cabinets.- 400 connectors, patch panels, and related network components.Quantities are planning estimates, not required purchase amounts. Vendors shall inspect existing infrastructure and propose appropriately sized solutions. Proposed switching equipment must support district network requirements, including appropriate PoE capacity, VLANs, routing, uplink connectivity, and compatibility with existing infrastructure.Proposals must identify equipment models, quantities, unit pricing, installation costs, required licensing, renewal costs, and any ineligible charges. Equivalent manufacturers and solutions will be considered. All equipment necessary for a complete, functional installation must be included.MANDATORY SITE VISIT:Vendors must schedule an individual site walk-through by emailing [redacted]. Appointments will be scheduled during normal business hours, subject to district availability, and must be completed by December 2, 2026. Vendors shall assess the applicable network closets and other installation locations. The district will provide reasonable opportunities to schedule visits. Failure to complete the mandatory walk-through will result in disqualification.BIDDING REQUIREMENTS:All questions must be submitted in writing by November 30, 2026. Written answers and material clarifications will be made available equally to prospective bidders through EPC.Proposals must be emailed to [redacted] by December 10, 2026, at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Late proposals will be disqualified. Vendor selection and contract award will not occur before the applicable Allowable Contract Date and stated bid deadline.Bids will be evaluated using a weighted matrix, with the price of eligible products and services as the most heavily weighted factor. The district reserves the right to award all, part, or none of the requested services and to make separate awards where appropriate.DISQUALIFYING FACTORS:1. Failure to complete the mandatory site walk-through by December 2, 2026.2. Failure to submit a complete proposal with equipment descriptions, quantities, and itemized pricing by the stated deadline.3. Proposed equipment must be new, compatible with existing district network infrastructure, and include applicable manufacturer warranties. Equivalent equipment must include sufficient documentation demonstrating equivalency.4. Bidders must provide their E-Rate SPIN or documentation that an application for one has been submitted.5. Contractors performing patch-panel retermination or related cabling work must provide evidence of appropriate insurance and any legally required bonding.6. Proposals must separately identify equipment, installation costs, required licensing, and any E-Rate-ineligible products or services.7. Service Provider Invoicing (SPI) is mandatory. The awarded vendor must agree in writing to provide discounted billing and submit FCC Form 474 directly to USAC for the eligible funded portion. The district will pay only its non-discounted share and any applicable ineligible costs. Vendors unwilling to provide SPI billing will be disqualified. BEAR reimbursement billing will not be accepted.Proposals must include all necessary components and services for the proposed switching infrastructure to operate as described. The district is not obligated to purchase the maximum estimated quantities.

service_requests.function: Uninterruptable Power Supply/Battery Backup and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: East Liverpool City Schools seeks bids for up to 20 network UPS/battery backup systems across five eligible schools and approximately 14 network closets. The project includes UPS units, batteries, network management, necessary software/licenses, mounting accessories, installation, configuration, and testing. Ubiquiti or equivalent solutions will be considered.Most district buildings have backup generators. Vendors must verify generator-supported circuits and size UPS systems to maintain network operation during generator startup and transfer. Westgate Middle School has no generator and may require extended battery runtime.Vendors shall assess network power loads, runtime requirements, electrical compatibility, and equipment eligibility. Quantities are estimates. Proposals must identify models, quantities, unit prices, expected runtime, warranties, installation costs, licensing, and ineligible charges. UPS systems supporting ineligible equipment must be identified for cost allocation.MANDATORY SITE VISIT:Vendors must schedule an individual site visit by emailing [redacted]. Visits must be completed by December 2, 2026. Reasonable scheduling opportunities will be provided. Failure to complete the visit is disqualifying.BIDDING REQUIREMENTS:Written questions are due November 30, 2026. Material answers and clarifications will be shared equally through EPC. Email proposals to [redacted] by December 10, 2026, at 2:00 PM ET. Late bids will be disqualified. No selection or award will occur before the Allowable Contract Date and bid deadline.Bids will be evaluated using a weighted matrix, with eligible price as the most heavily weighted factor. The district may award all, part, or none of the request.DISQUALIFYING FACTORS:1. Failure to complete the mandatory site visit by December 2, 2026.2. Late or materially incomplete bids lacking equipment descriptions or itemized pricing.3. Equipment must be new, compatible with district requirements, and include applicable manufacturer warranties. Equivalent products must include supporting specifications.4. Bidders must provide an E-Rate SPIN or documentation of an application.5. Installation contractors must provide evidence of applicable insurance and legally required bonding.6. Bids must separately identify equipment, installation, required licensing, and ineligible costs.7. SPI discounted billing is mandatory. The awarded vendor must agree in writing to submit FCC Form 474 to USAC for the funded portion. The district pays its non-discounted share and ineligible costs. Vendors refusing SPI billing will be disqualified. BEAR billing will not be accepted.All purchases are subject to applicable E-Rate eligibility rules. Maximum estimated quantities are not required purchase amounts.

East Liverpool City Schools requests FY2027 bids for eligible MIBS, BMIC, and software/licenses for existing district-owned Extreme Networks equipment at five schools. These are contingency requests if the district does not complete its separately bid wireless and switching replacements. The district may buy all, part, or none of the services and may award categories separately.Existing inventory (estimated): 50 switches (stacked and standalone), 230 wireless APs, and 1 wireless controller. Bidders shall verify equipment and identify covered models and quantities. No new hardware is requested on this Form 470.MIBS: Quote eligible ongoing operation, monitoring, and management of existing internal broadband equipment, with support hours, response times, and service scope.BMIC: Separately quote eligible repair, upkeep, troubleshooting, and in-person/on-site configuration work.SOFTWARE/LICENSING: Separately quote eligible ExtremeCloud IQ or compatible licenses and associated eligible software/remote support for existing APs, switches, and controller. Identify license terms, quantities, renewals, and equipment covered. Licenses must be available independently of MIBS or BMIC. Avoid duplicate charges and separately itemize ineligible costs. Newly purchased replacement equipment is excluded.MANDATORY ASSESSMENTS:For bids involving MIBS or on-site BMIC, vendors must arrange and complete a district site assessment by December 2, 2026, emailing [redacted] to schedule during business hours. Licensing-only bidders may complete a remote inventory review instead. The district will provide reasonable scheduling opportunities and equivalent baseline information to bidders. Failure to complete the applicable assessment by the deadline is disqualifying.BIDDING REQUIREMENTS:Questions are due in writing November 30, 2026. Material answers and clarifications will be shared equally through EPC.Email bids to [redacted] by December 10, 2026, at 2:00 PM ET. Late bids are disqualified. No award will occur before both the Allowable Contract Date and bid deadline.Bids will be evaluated using a weighted matrix with the price of eligible products and services as the most heavily weighted factor. The district may award MIBS, BMIC, and licensing separately.DISQUALIFYING FACTORS:1. Failure to complete the applicable assessment by December 2, 2026.2. Late or materially incomplete proposals lacking service descriptions or itemized pricing.3. Failure to provide an E-Rate SPIN or documentation of an application for one.4. Failure to separately identify MIBS, BMIC, software/licensing, and applicable ineligible costs.5. Refusal to provide Service Provider Invoicing (SPI) discounted billing. Awarded vendors must invoice USAC using FCC Form 474 for the funded portion. The district will pay its non-discounted share and ineligible charges. BEAR reimbursement billing will not be accepted.All purchases and reimbursement are subject to the applicable FY2027 Eligible Services List and E-Rate requirements. No purchase or service award is guaranteed.

There are no state or local restrictions or regulations on how service providers can contact the District's technology or business manager. Arizona State Procurement Code requires a formal sealed bidding process; or purchasing from an IGA, State Master Contract, other approved cooperative purchasing contract, or compliant consortium procured contract for any procurement in excess of $100,000.00. Any quote/proposal whose total value exceeds $100,000.00 and is not linked to a current State Master Contract, other approved cooperative purchasing contract, or a compliant consortium procured contract will be disqualified by Arizona State Procurement Code. Any quotes must  comply with the underlying state master/cooperative purchasing agreement in pricing and terms. Any quote/proposal submitted that does not specifically address the services requested, is generic in nature or otherwise does not meet the requirements contained in this Form 470 and associated specifications may be considered non-responsive and may be disqualified. SPAM and/or robotic responses will not be considered valid bid responses and will be disqualified from consideration. All original contracts offered that are less than a 60 month term should include specifications that allow for annual one year extensions and/or month to month extensions at the discretion of the applicant; not to exceed a total of 60 months. Please quote all eligible and ineligible products/services separately. Any pricing proposed must comply with the FCC Lowest Corresponding Price Rule as required by the Universal Service First Report and Order, and restated in the FCC E-Rate Modernization Report and Order, adopted July 11, 2014. The FCC Lowest Corresponding Price rule prohibits an E-rate services offeror from offering or charging E-rate applicants a price higher than the lowest price that the offeror charges to non-residential customers who are similarly situated to a particular school, library, rural health care provider or consortium that purchase directly from the offeror.

Firewall Service, Components, and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: Category 2Funding Year 2027Riverside CSD BEN: 132390 is requesting bids for the following E-Rate Category 2 eligible hardware & licensing.Firewall (Licensing Only)(3 Units) Fortigate Firewall License - FC-10-F200F-950-02-12 (or equivalent)Data Transport Switch(1 Unit)  Unifi Switch 24P - Pro XG 24 PoE USW-Pro-XG-24-PoE (720W)(or equivalent)(1 Unit) Unifi Switch 48P - Pro XG 48 PoE USW-Pro-XG-48-PoE (1080W) (or equivalent)Bids must itemize:(a). cost of equipment(b). cost of installation separately for each equipment grouping, if applicable; and (c). cost of taxes/fees/shipping, if applicable. Bids shall include specific make and model of equipment, as well as the SKU of each piece of equipment. Bids must specify terms of the manufacturers warranty and what the license term is (if applicable). Any cost ineligible for E-Rate reimbursement must be clearly identified and itemized on the bid.If submitting a bid for equipment that is or equivalent to equipment listed on this form 470, the service provider shall submit evidence of equivalency.  The applicant will make a final determination of equivalence and interoperability with existing equipment.The make/model bid(s) must be for new equipment that is the most current model(s) available.If the bid includes software licenses, the bid shall designate whether the licenses are internal connections (IC) or if the software licenses are basic maintenance of internal connections (BMIC).If the bid includes installation for new equipment, the bid must specify the installers city and state.Bid evaluations may include points for service providers with a local presence or office within 150 miles. Bid evaluations may include points for service providers who provide a complete solution. e.g., the bid presented is inclusive of all requested components and services. Bidders must be willing to provide E-Rate discounted billing (form 474/SPI invoicing) and to include this statement in the proposal.Robo-bids and bids sent as SPAM without regard to products and services listed on the Form 470 and/or the RFP will be disqualified and will not be evaluated.The applicant reserves the right to cancel this request for bids and to reject all related proposals.Prices need to be held firm through the duration of the 2027 E-Rate Category 2 installation period (from date of bid to September 30, 2028).This project is dependent upon receiving an E-Rate funding commitment decision letter.The deadline for service provider proposals is 9:00 am Central time, 29 days after the date this Form 470 is posted.  Bid evaluation may take place anytime after the deadline for proposals up to the last day of the E-Rate funding window.The applicant reserves the right to reject late-submitted proposals. No phone calls or texts. For documentation purposes all communication is required to be via email. Proposals must be e-mailed to the Form 470 contact. [redacted]

service_requests.function: Wireless Access Points and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: School seeks bids on up to 75 Wireless Access points providing wifi-7 service, with a mix of both indoor and outdoor models.  School may need fewer and requests vendors provide a scheduled walk-through to identify needs, best model options, determine compatibility with existing network, etc.  Quotes must include all necessary optics, modules, licenses, software, installation, configuration, setup, etc. or otherwise as needed for functionality.  Vendor must break out cost for each item quoted and list manufacturer part numbers, quantity and price for each.  Please note that equivalent equipment must show compatibility with existing network structure. All projects are subject to eRate fundability and Board approval.  All questions and bids are to be directed to the tech contact listed below.  School reserves the right to reduce project(s) after seeing quotes where eRate funding and budgets are impacted.  Vendors who would like to do a site visit must schedule with the tech contact; no walk-in site visits will be permitted. Vendor must be an eRate eligible provider with active SPIN listed on their bid and must adhere to all state and local guidelines and restrictions. Vendors are required by USAC to maintain sam.gov registration and maintain updated compliance paperwork with USAC; vendors who are not currently compliant may be eliminated from consideration.   SPAM and/or robotic responses will not be considered valid bid responses and will be disqualified from consideration. All bids submitted prior to the applicants vendor selection will be given equal consideration, with no award made before the close of the 28-day posting period.

Internet Access and Data Transmission Service
Switches and Necessary Software and Licenses
service_requests.description: District seeks bids on the following network equipment:(1) up to six (6) switches equivalent to Cisco Catalyst 9200 series 48-port PoE with any applicable licensing.(2) up to fifty (50) LICENSES for existing Extreme Networks Wireless Access points. Please price 3- and 5-year options.  District is not seeking replacement equipment.Quotes must include all necessary optics, modules, licenses, software, installation, configuration, setup, etc. or otherwise as needed for functionality.  Vendor must break out cost for each item quoted and list manufacturer part numbers, quantity and price for each.  Please note that equivalent equipment must show compatibility with existing network structure. All projects are subject to eRate fundability and Board approval.  School reserves the right to reduce project(s) after seeing quotes where eRate funding and budgets are impacted.  All questions and bids are to be directed to the tech contact listed below.    Vendors who would like to do a site visit must schedule with the tech contact; no walk-in site visits will be permitted. Vendor must be an eRate eligible provider with active SPIN listed on their bid and must adhere to all state and local guidelines and restrictions. Vendors are required by USAC to maintain sam.gov registration and maintain updated compliance paperwork with USAC; vendors who are not currently compliant may be eliminated from consideration.   SPAM and/or robotic responses will not be considered valid bid responses and will be disqualified from consideration. All bids submitted prior to the applicants vendor selection will be given equal consideration, with no award made before the close of the 28-day posting period.

service_requests.function: Internet Access and Data Transmission Service
service_requests.description: School seeks bids on the following equipment: (A) Up to 60 Wireless Access points - must be WiFi 7+ with a preference for UniFi or Ruckus brands. (B) Up to 5 switches - both 24- and 48-port Gigabit with 10GB uplinks, Managed, PoE+, prefer Unifi or Ruckus. (C) Up to 5 UPS units, 1500VA+.  Quotes must include all necessary optics, modules, licenses, software, installation, configuration, setup, etc. or otherwise as needed for functionality.  Vendor must break out cost for each item quoted and list manufacturer part numbers, quantity and price for each.  Please note that equivalent equipment must show compatibility with existing network structure. All projects are subject to eRate fundability and Board approval.  School reserves the right to reduce project(s) after seeing quotes where eRate funding and budgets are impacted.  All questions and bids are to be directed to the tech contact listed below.    Vendors who would like to do a site visit must schedule with the tech contact; no walk-in site visits will be permitted. Vendor must be an eRate eligible provider with active SPIN listed on their bid and must adhere to all state and local guidelines and restrictions. Vendors are required by USAC to maintain sam.gov registration and maintain updated compliance paperwork with USAC; vendors who are not currently compliant may be eliminated from consideration.   SPAM and/or robotic responses will not be considered valid bid responses and will be disqualified from consideration. All bids submitted prior to the applicants vendor selection will be given equal consideration, with no award made before the close of the 28-day posting period.

service_requests.description: District seeks quotes on up to 15 UPS units, and for up to 25 PoE or PoE+ switches as follows: mix of 24 and 48 port models along with necessary licenses. Current environment is Meraki and any proposed equipment should be compatible with the existing infrastructure.  Quotes must include all necessary optics, modules, licenses, software, installation, configuration, setup, etc. or otherwise as needed for functionality.  Vendor must break out cost for each item quoted and list manufacturer part numbers, quantity and price for each.  Please note that equivalent equipment must show compatibility with existing network structure. All projects are subject to eRate fundability and Board approval.  School reserves the right to reduce project(s) after seeing quotes where eRate funding and budgets are impacted.  All questions and bids are to be directed to the tech contact listed below.    Vendors who would like to do a site visit must schedule with the tech contact; no walk-in site visits will be permitted. Vendor must be an eRate eligible provider with active SPIN listed on their bid and must adhere to all state and local guidelines and restrictions. Vendors are required by USAC to maintain sam.gov registration and maintain updated compliance paperwork with USAC; vendors who are not currently compliant may be eliminated from consideration.   SPAM and/or robotic responses will not be considered valid bid responses and will be disqualified from consideration. All bids submitted prior to the applicants vendor selection will be given equal consideration, with no award made before the close of the 28-day posting period.

service_requests.description: Robo Bids: Because the requested services are complex and specific, we require that all bids be submitted manually by an authorized vendor representative and include the necessary documentation, pricing, and terms. Bids submitted through automated systems without a tailored manual response will not be accepted. All vendors must ensure that their proposals accurately reflect a full understanding of the RFP requirements.  Proposals may provide either a direct 1:1 replacement of the existing infrastructure or their own design.   All proposals should be designed for optimal performance in relation to the requirements across all applicant facilities. Site Survey: An in-person site walk of all locations will be made available November 18th, between 9 a.m.- 3 p.m.  Please complete Appendix C: Intent to Bid to register for the site walk-through. No more than two [2] employees per vendor. Requirements	Supply of new Wireless Access Points (WAPs).	Mounting hardware and brackets	Wireless LAN controller(s) or cloud-based management platform.	Configuration and deployment services.	Reconfiguration of the applicants ClearPass onboarding platform, or an equivalent solution.	Testing and validation of coverage and performance.	Documentation and training for applicant IT staff.	Ongoing support and maintenance for 5 years.	*Optional* vendors may bid on installation services for access points. Invoices must include all charges separated by line items, including any applicable taxes and fees. Invoices must identify eligible and ineligible items. Respondents who bundle eligible and ineligible costs into a single line item to hide ineligible items will be fully responsible for any resulting loss of funds. The evaluation of proposals is a two-tiered process. Tier One consists of an administrative review of compliance with mandatory requirements listed above. The Applicant or Agent scores all Tier One components either pass or fail, and a Proposer must pass all requirements to move to the next Tier. service_requests.description: The Pomeroy Public Library is seeking bids for eligible broadband internal connections as well as managed internal broadband services for firewall services and components which are separate from our standard firewall protection. The library is asking for service providers to list any software support, equipment, and also eligible expenses including the management and operation of the LAN/WLAN, including installation, activation, and initial configuration of eligible components and on-site training on the use of eligible equipment. Equipment or services produced or provided by a company that the FCC has designated as a national security threat to the integrity of communications networks or the communications supply chain are not eligible for E-Rate support. Therefore, all bids must comply with national security standards. Firewall protection that is provided by a vendor other than the Internet access service provider or priced out separately will be considered a Category Two internal connections component. Bids should be posted to [redacted] within 29 days from the date this Form 470 is certified. Any bids received after that date may be excluded for consideration by the Library Director.

service_requests.description: Caddo Parish School District (BEN 139307) requests competitive proposals for E-Rate Funding Year 2027 Category Two network electronics, associated software and licensing, installation, and eligible maintenance services, as described in RFP 02-27 Network Electronics and its attachments.The District seeks approximately 2,500 wireless access points with associated five-year licensing, approximately 175 48-port PoE network switches with associated network modules, power supplies, stacking components, optical transceivers, software licensing, and related accessories, or functionally equivalent products meeting the RFP requirements.The solicitation also includes eligible manufacturer maintenance and support for designated existing and proposed network equipment, subject to the specifications and eligibility allocations in the RFP.Installation services may include equipment removal and replacement, rack mounting, installation of components, transfer and management of existing cabling, and verification of equipment operation and connectivity.The District anticipates phased purchases under an initial one-year contract with two optional one-year renewals. All quantities are estimates, and no minimum purchase is guaranteed. Vendors must provide itemized pricing and separately identify E-Rate-eligible and ineligible costs.All proposals must comply with RFP 02-27, including its bid submission instructions, deadlines, technical specifications, evaluation criteria, and contractual conditions. The actual RFP and all applicable attachments are incorporated into this request.

service_requests.description: Please review RFP carefully.MIBS was listed above in case USAC deems any of the necessary software licenses to fit that category.Project ScopeThe Applicant seeks eligible equipment as outlined in Appendix A.  Equipment shall be new, factory-sealed equipment currently available from the manufacturer; the Applicant will not accept proposals of used, remanufactured, refurbished, "B stock", returns, open-box, discontinued, "gray market," or equipment in any other condition other than new and factory-sealed with all original manufacturer warranties.Installation will be in place of existing equipment and the requested equipment will be integrated into the existing environment.  Each bid should include all labor necessary for staging, installation, testing, and documentation of equipment. Equipment staging will consist of (but not be limited to) ensuring firmware version consistency, configuration loading, and hardware preparation for mounting.  Software and firmware version for components will be agreed upon at time of deployment, and configurations will be coordinated with the Applicants staff.  Installation by the selected vendor shall include the removal of the existing equipment and placement of the new equipment.  Equipment testing should verify access to internal resources and the Internet. Documentation should include configuration and summary reports of installations.  Installation can be performed from a ladder in most cases; for a small number of APs, a lift will be required. Questions/Site VisitsNo informational meetings or building visits will be scheduled.   Any questions related to the technical aspects of this document should be directed to David Figg, Technology Director at [redacted], no later than 2:00 pm (EST) on 11-13-2026. Answers to any written questions or any additional information, revisions, or clarifications to the RFP will be provided in the form of an addendum to be posted with the FCC Form 470 on the Universal Service (E-Rate) website.  It is the sole responsibility of the Service Provider to check for any addenda that may be issued.Proposal DeliveryThe Applicant reserves the right to reject each and every bid, and to waive informalities, irregularities, and errors in the bidding to the extent permitted by law.  This includes the right to extend the date and time for receipt of bids.  In the event that a responsible bid is not received or if it is determined that the low bid received is too high, the bid received will be rejected and the project will be cancelled or re-bid.  Bid should be emailed to the office of David Figg, Technology Director, at [redacted], by 12-15-2026 at 2:00 pm(EST).APPENDIX ABelow is a reference of the type of equipment and capacities (or their equivalent) to be supplied.   Bidders should price separately and clearly indicate any ineligible costs for all services and equipment associated with this RFP.   For any part numbers that have been updated or replaced by the manufacturer, bidders should offer the most similar current part.Please see RFP for Appendix A

service_requests.description: Empire Union School District is seeking pricing for wireless network equipment and installation for a districtwide wireless upgrade, including approximately 229 wireless access points, mounts, one wireless controller, licensing, installation, configuration and support. For a complete description of the requested equipment and services, please refer to the District-issued Request for Proposal #2027-WIRELESS, EUSD Wireless Network Equipment. service_requests.description: Seeking bids on Ubiquiti USW-ENTERPRISE-24POE or equivalent.  Equivalent switches must include at least 24 ports, must support gigabit transmission on all ports, must support 2.5 Gbps+ on at least 10 ports, must support 10 Gbps on uplink port.  Any equivalent bid must also include any and all licensing necessary to use switch for a minimum of five years.  Bids including products that fail to meet these requirements, or bidders failing to meet these requirements, may be disqualified.  Bids must be submitted via email to the contact listed on this Form 470 by 5pm Atlantic Time on December 16, 2026.

service_requests.description: *** IMPORTANT NOTE:  This Form 470 is an expansion of the scope associated with 2027 Fullerton ESD Form 470 # 270001338. During the job walk, an additional 125K feet of cabling and upgraded patch panels was identified. This Form 470 increases the cabling from 525K feet to 650K feet of cabling and adds 350 Cat6a patch panels. Due date for the RFP and all other factors remain the same. Documentation is duplicated here and on the original Form 470.PROJECT BACKGROUNDBased on an average estimated length of 150 feet per cable run, the project represents approximately 650,000 feet of Cat6A cabling.2. SCOPE OF WORKThe District is seeking proposals from qualified contractors to furnish and install Category 6A (Cat6A) network cabling and associated infrastructure at designated locations across its twenty (20) school sites. The project consists of an estimated 1,750 network data drops, with two (2) individual Cat6A cable runs per drop, totaling approximately 3,500 cable runs.The District will determine final installation locations and quantities based on site conditions and operational needs. The District has provided supplemental attachments identifying estimated network data drops by school and classroom type, along with anticipated raceway lengths by room type. These estimates are provided for bidding and planning purposes. Contractors shall account for the necessary materials, labor, and installation requirements within their proposed pricing.A. Network Data Drop Requirements1. Each completed network data drop shall consist of two (2) independent Cat6A cable runs originating from the designated Main Distribution Frame (MDF) or Intermediate Distribution Frame (IDF). 2. Each drop shall terminate into two (2) black Cat6A-rated RJ45 keystone jacks installed in a single two-port faceplate. Black jacks shall distinguish the newCat6A installations from existing cabling. 3. Classrooms are generally expected to receive two (2) new data drops, typically on opposite sides of the room Existing drops designated for replacement shall be removed and replaced as part of the installation. Where a second drop does not currently exist, the contractor shall provide the necessary new cabling and pathway to complete the installation. 4. Additional installations may include offices, libraries, multipurpose rooms, and other District-designated locations. Final placement shall be coordinated with District IT staff.5. All cable runs shall comply with applicable Cat6A performance requirements, including industry-standard channel length limitations and applicable Power over Ethernet (PoE) requirements.B. Existing Cabling Removal and Replacement 1. The project shall include the removal and replacement of designated existing Category 5 (Cat5) cabling associated with the new installations.2. The contractor shall remove existing cables, jacks, faceplates, and termination being replaced, including accessible abandoned or disconnected cabling associated with the designated replacement locations 3. Existing active cabling not designated for replacement shall remain intact and operational. 4. Existing suitable pathways may be reused for new Cat6A installations.1. All new Cat6A cable runs shall terminate at the designated MDF or IDF using compatible Cat6A-rated patch-panel connections. 2. Existing compatible Cat6A patch panels may be utilized where sufficient available ports exist, subject to District IT approval. 3. Where additional capacity is required, the contractor shall furnish and install modular Cat6A-rated RJ45-to-RJ45 pass-through patch panels, utilizing inline couplers with RJ45 connections on both the front and rear, without traditional punch-down (IDC) terminations. All necessary couplers, mounting hardware, labeling, and cable management shall be included and compatible with existing District rack infrastructure. Rear cable terminations shall utilize manufacturer-approved Cat6A-rated RJ45 connectors compatible with the pass-through couplers and meet applicable Cat6A certification requirements. 4. The contractor shall provide one (1) blue Cat6A patch cable per individual cable run at the MDF/IDF. Patch cables shall generally be one foot (1') in length, with lengths up to three feet (3') provided where necessary to accommodate rack configurations and connection locations. All patch cables shall be factory-terminated, appropriately rated, and compatible with the installed infrastructure. Required cable lengths shall be included in the proposed pricing. 5. All new cabling shall be neatly routed, supported, organized, and labeled. Affected patch panels, cable managers, racks, and associated infrastructure shall be left clean, accessible, and properly organized.6. Existing copper, fiber connections, and other active infrastructure shall remain intact and operational unless otherwise authorized by the District.

All new Cat6A cable runs shall terminate at the designated MDF or IDF using compatible Cat6A-rated patch-panel connections. 2. Existing compatible Cat6A patch panels may be utilized where sufficient available ports exist, subject to District IT approval. 3. Where additional capacity is required, the contractor shall furnish and install modular Cat6A-rated RJ45-to-RJ45 pass-through patch panels, utilizing inline couplers with RJ45 connections on both the front and rear, without traditional punch-down (IDC) terminations. All necessary couplers, mounting hardware, labeling, and cable management shall be included and compatible with existing District rack infrastructure. Rear cable terminations shall utilize manufacturer-approved Cat6A-rated RJ45 connectors compatible with the pass-through couplers and meet applicable Cat6A certification requirements. 4. The contractor shall provide one (1) blue Cat6A patch cable per individual cable run at the MDF/IDF. Patch cables shall generally be one foot (1') in length, with lengths up to three feet (3') provided where necessary to accommodate rack configurations and connection locations. All patch cables shall be factory-terminated, appropriately rated, and compatible with the installed infrastructure. Required cable lengths shall be included in the proposed pricing. 5. All new cabling shall be neatly routed, supported, organized, and labeled. Affected patch panels, cable managers, racks, and associated infrastructure shall be left clean, accessible, and properly organized.6. Existing copper, fiber connections, and other active infrastructure shall remain intact and operational unless otherwise authorized by the District.
